statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk is low at 10% while Stress is elevated at 56%; the shared Nasdaq-100 reading applies jointly to NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD.
recommendation: Conditions map to the EA_ON band. Observed overnight structure is two-sided and range-bound, so Tail remains well below the block threshold despite an elevated-Stress cross-asset backdrop. The narrow danger window spans 13:30-15:00 UTC around the US cash open and the 14:00 UTC ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS releases.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold a narrow overnight range with VIX near 15, against firm crude and the highest 10-year yield since January 2025
body: NQ futures trade near 29,465, about -0.16%, inside a roughly 88-point overnight range (29,434.75-29,522.50) with repeated two-sided rotation and no observed directional efficiency. E-mini S&P 500 futures are similarly contained at 7,692.25, about -0.09%, in a 17-point band, and gold is flat near $4,477. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Monday at 29,456.97, up 0.08%, off a session low of 29,304.49, outperforming the S&P 500 at -0.33% and the Dow at -0.70%. The cross-asset backdrop stays risk-negative but orderly: US forces struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz and Iran fired missiles at US bases in Jordan, lifting Brent above $90 and WTI to about $86.91 (+1.34% overnight), while the 10-year Treasury yield closed at 4.758%, its highest since January 2025, and the 2-year stood at 4.34% in the latest H.15 release. Against that, VIX finished at 14.92, low in absolute terms, and index internals showed rotation rather than one-way structure: the SOX gained 0.57% with the semiconductor complex broadly higher, while megacap performance was widely dispersed with five of eight names lower. That combination - a contained price path, low implied volatility and high internal dispersion - keeps Tail low at 10%. Stress is held at 56% by the unresolved Hormuz backdrop, the crude premium, the elevated long end, and a same-day stack of two high-impact US releases. Confidence is high at 88% on fresh verified price-path, volatility, yield, energy and calendar evidence. No new escalation had been verified between the Monday US close and this assessment. Conditional risk concentrates around the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 14:00 UTC ISM Manufacturing PMI (consensus 55.2) and JOLTS job openings (consensus 7.33M), where forecast Tail peaks at 18% and dominant mode is projected as event/whipsaw, still inside the EA_ON band.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment and every one sat in the EA_ON band, with Tail between 5 and 17 and Stress rising from the mid 30s to 56. The single Tail peak of 17 came in the 09:00 UTC hour on August 31 during a European event/whipsaw window. From the US session onward Stress climbed steadily as crude extended on the Larak Island exchange and the 10-year yield pushed to its highest level since January 2025, while Tail stayed compressed between 9 and 13 because the price path itself remained two-sided. Dominant mode was mixed in 22 of 24 hours, with event/whipsaw only in the 09:00 and 10:00 UTC European window. The overnight hours since the Monday cash close repeated that pattern: a narrow range, no session-extreme holding and no failed-retracement sequence.
outlookSummary: The base case over the next 24 hours is continued contained, two-sided trade with an elevated-Stress, low-Tail profile. Conditional risk concentrates in a narrow band around the 13:30 UTC US cash open and the simultaneous 14:00 UTC ISM Manufacturing PMI and JOLTS releases, where forecast Tail peaks at 18 and Stress at 66, with dominant mode projected as event/whipsaw - still below the block band. Risk is projected to decay through the US afternoon as event volatility unwinds, with a small power-hour uptick, before returning to the low end of the range overnight into the Asian session. Every forecast hour maps to EA_ON. The projection would be invalidated by observed persistent one-way structure: repeated extension after failed retracements, NQ holding near session extremes, or a delayed post-release second leg. A fresh Hormuz discontinuity is the main channel capable of overriding this path outside the scheduled calendar.
